Finding: Provider placeholder interpolation allowed any server-managed secret (including ADMIN_PASSWORD, VICI_API_PASS and AMI_SECRET) into provider settings/payloads.
Evidence: src/env-store.ts interpolateEnvPlaceholders + MANAGED_SECRET_KEYS; operator-editable provider prompt/endpoint fields
Impact: A non-owner operator could exfiltrate the console admin password or PBX credentials to an external provider endpoint.
Remediation: Separate provider-only allowlist (interpolateProviderPlaceholders) limited to provider keys, speech-service URL/key and non-secret routing values; admin/PBX secrets rejected.
Verification: tests/backend-audit-verify.ts asserts ADMIN_PASSWORD/VICI_API_PASS/AMI_SECRET/CUSTOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET never appear while provider keys and SPEECH_SERVICE_URL still resolve.

Finding: Secret masking returned first and last four characters, including for ADMIN_PASSWORD.
Evidence: src/env-store.ts maskSecret old implementation; /api/state exposes masked values to viewers/operators; public/app.js buildCloudSecretsStatus masked browser-local secrets the same way
Impact: Partial disclosure reduced the effective entropy of every configured secret and exposed admin-password fragments.
Remediation: Server and static-demo masks are now always a fixed 8-dot string; no characters of the value are returned.
Verification: tests/backend-audit-verify.ts checks maskSecret and getSecretsStatus for ADMIN_PASSWORD and DEEPGRAM_API_KEY; static-console suite passes after the app.js change.

Finding: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Permissions-Policy or HSTS headers were set by the Node server.
Impact: Higher impact from any injected script, MIME sniffing, clickjacking/framing and unnecessary device permissions; no HSTS on TLS deployments.
Remediation: Added CSP (self, Deepgram connect, Google Fonts, object-src none, frame-ancestors none), nosniff, frame DENY, microphone-only Permissions-Policy and conditional HSTS when req.secure.
Verification: Live curl of /health/live and /login shows all headers; tests/backend-audit-verify.ts asserts CSP/nosniff/frame/powered-by.

Finding: Login throttle used the proxy socket address instead of the trusted client IP, so every operator behind nginx/ALB shared one 30/min bucket.
Evidence: src/server.ts login throttle keyed on req.socket.remoteAddress
Impact: A single abusive client could lock all operators out of login; per-client attempts were not isolated.
Remediation: Throttle now keys on req.ip after the existing trust-proxy resolution.
Verification: npm test (security + backend-audit) passes; live reverse-proxy smoke remains manual on EC2.

Finding: Signed-in visit to /login?next=/login or /signup redirected back into the same page, creating a loop.
Impact: Browser redirect loop; confusing login state.
Remediation: safeNextPath now rejects /login, /login.html and /signup targets.
Verification: Live curl with session cookie returned 302 Location: /; backend-audit regression asserts it.

Finding: AWS and ViciBox systemd units ran the Node service as root with no sandboxing.
Impact: A server compromise or dependency RCE gained full host privileges; recordings/.env were root-owned.
Remediation: Both units now use a dedicated voiceagent user plus NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp/Devices, ProtectSystem/Home, kernel/control-group protection, UMask 0077; deploy script creates/chowns the account.
Verification: Static review + bash -n; systemd execution is an EC2 runbook step, not reproducible in this sandbox.

Finding: Docker image ran as UID 1000 but listened on privileged port 533, so the container could not bind and never started.
Evidence: Dockerfile ENV PORT=533 / EXPOSE 533 with USER appuser
Impact: docker run failed with EACCES; the shipped container path was non-functional.
Remediation: PORT/EXPOSE moved to 8080, /data volume added for VAC_DATA_DIR, healthcheck added on /health/live.
Verification: docker build/run unavailable in this sandbox (Docker is not installed); Dockerfile statically reviewed and README commands updated.

Finding: tools/start-demo.js downloaded cloudflared over http and followed arbitrary redirects with no size or host bound.
Impact: A compromised redirect or MITM could deliver an arbitrary executable; unbounded download could fill disk.
Remediation: Download now requires https, allowlists github.com/objects.githubusercontent.com/release-assets.githubusercontent.com, uses a 30 s timeout and 100 MiB cap.
Verification: node --check tools/start-demo.js; mirror logic in src/demo-tunnel.ts already had these guards.

Finding: No per-request CSRF token; protection relies on same-origin Origin checks and SameSite cookies.
Impact: A non-browser or Origin-less client that already holds a session cookie is not distinguishable from a legitimate integration; browser CSRF depends on current browser SameSite/Origin behavior.
Remediation: Add a double-submit or session-bound CSRF token for state-changing routes if non-browser clients must be supported.
Verification: Origin-bearing cross-site requests are covered by tests/security-verify.ts; Origin-less requests remain accepted by design.

Finding: No MFA, breached-password screening, idle timeout, or per-account login throttling; sessions last 7 days.
Impact: Stolen passwords/session cookies remain usable for up to 7 days; no second factor.
Remediation: Add TOTP/WebAuthn, breach-list check, configurable shorter/idle session expiry and per-account lockout.
Verification: Not implemented; documented as a known gap in docs/security/AUTHENTICATION-AUTHORIZATION-AUDIT.md.

Finding: Login and API throttles are in-process maps; a multi-worker or multi-instance deployment multiplies the limit and loses state on restart.
Impact: Distributed brute force can exceed the intended rate; restart resets counters.
Remediation: Use a shared store (Redis) or a single trusted edge/WAF rate limit in production.
Verification: Single-process tests pass; deployment guidance should state one instance or edge limiting.

Finding: Custom webhooks can target loopback/private addresses (SSRF surface) by design for local CRM/PBX integrations.
Evidence: src/webhook-executor.ts; docs note local HTTP support
Impact: An owner/admin who can edit functions could reach internal services; role-gated but not host-restricted.
Remediation: For internet-facing deployments, add an allowlist/deny-private-IP mode or a separate egress proxy; keep webhook editing owner/admin-only.
Verification: Existing tests cover header/lead interpolation, redirect rejection and response-size limits, not network allowlisting.

Finding: All accounts share one console state and all recordings; roles gate actions, not records.
Impact: An operator/viewer can read every agent prompt, campaign and browser/bridge recording.
Remediation: Add tenant/owner scoping or separate instances per customer; document retention and access expectations.
Verification: Documented in README and docs/security/AUTHENTICATION-AUTHORIZATION-AUDIT.md; no code change.

Finding: Legacy ADMIN_PASSWORD creates a static owner-equivalent session with no account identity; it cannot be revoked per user.
Impact: Shared password cannot be attributed or selectively revoked; logout-all does revoke its sessions.
Remediation: Prefer named owner accounts; keep ADMIN_PASSWORD only for bootstrap/recovery and rotate it after creating owners.
Verification: Existing security tests cover bootstrap, revocation and logout-all.

Finding: VICIdial non-agent/agent API credentials are sent as URL query parameters, as required by the VICIdial API.
Impact: The pass value can appear in local proxy/Asterisk logs; audit log masks it.
Remediation: Keep VICIdial on loopback/private network, restrict proxy logging and rotate the API user password.
Verification: maskUrl is applied to audit entries; tests cover API audit shape.

Finding: Recordings and SQLite state are not encrypted at rest; all signed-in accounts can download them.
Impact: Host/volume/backup access exposes call audio and transcripts.
Remediation: Use encrypted EBS volumes, restrictive filesystem permissions, backup encryption and retention policy.
Verification: Files are owner-only where supported; encryption is an infrastructure control, not implemented in app.

Finding: CSP still needs script-src/style-src 'unsafe-inline' because the shipped UI uses inline handlers/styles.
Impact: CSP does not fully mitigate injected inline script; it still blocks external script origins and framing.
Remediation: Move remaining inline handlers/styles to files and adopt nonces/hashes before tightening the policy.
Verification: CSP header verified live; no functional break observed in npm test.

Finding: public/index.html had one extra closing and an orphaned ambient-canvas comment.
Impact: Invalid DOM nesting can misplace the header/layout and break future HTML parsing assumptions.
Remediation: Removed the stray closing tag and empty comment wrapper.
Verification: html-validate no longer reports close-order; docs mirror re-synced.

Finding: Six modal/login buttons lacked type=button and one close button used an inline onclick handler.
Impact: Buttons could act as implicit submit controls; inline handler bypassed the delegated event path.
Remediation: Added type=button, aria-label on the icon close button, and bound keys-close-x in app.js.
Verification: html-validate reports no implicit-button-type; static-console tests pass.

Finding: EACCES fallback for the default privileged port 533 was dead code: listenWithFallback was called with retriesLeft=0.
Impact: A non-root Linux user following the README got EACCES and no server, despite a logged promise of automatic fallback.
Remediation: Fallback now enabled only for EACCES on ports <1024; EADDRINUSE still fails fast; the chosen port is exported.
Verification: Live run with E2B_SANDBOX unset and PORT=533 logged EACCES then listened on 5533; EADDRINUSE remains fatal by design.

Finding: PORT was parsed with Number(PORT||533) without integer/range validation.
Impact: Values like 12.5, 70000 or empty strings produced confusing listen errors.
Remediation: PORT must be an integer 0-65535; invalid values log and exit 1.
Verification: Build + startup validation reviewed; normal 533/5533/8080 paths tested.

Finding: Shutdown called server.close() before closeAllConnections(), so keep-alive sockets delayed exit until the 10 s force timer.
Impact: Slow restarts/deploys and possible dropped calls during the forced exit.
Remediation: Close is initiated first, then idle/keep-alive connections are destroyed, then the close callback is awaited.
Verification: Live SIGTERM smoke exited cleanly; npm test server teardown passes.

Finding: LAN-IP detection skipped every 172.* address, which excludes normal EC2 VPC private addresses (172.16/12).
Impact: The public demo launcher could choose the wrong interface or fail to advertise a reachable EC2 address.
Remediation: Skip docker/veth/lo adapters by name instead of excluding 172.*; keep 172.31.x eligible.
Verification: Unit/static review; demo tunnel needs a real EC2 run to confirm the chosen address.

Finding: Active-tunnel detection probed metrics ports sequentially with a 1.1 s budget on every /api/state.
Impact: Up to ~1.1 s added latency to console state polling when no tunnel exists.
Remediation: Probes run in parallel with one bounded deadline.
Verification: Build + npm test; no behavioral regression in demo-tunnel status tests.

Finding: @types/express v5 was installed against Express 4, producing misleading types.
Impact: Type-checking could accept v5-only shapes the runtime does not support.
Remediation: Pinned @types/express ^4.17.25.
Verification: npm run build passes with strict/no-unused flags.

Finding: @types/node v20 was used while the runtime and docs require Node 22.5+.
Impact: Node 22 APIs (node:sqlite, fetch, closeAllConnections) were typed against an older surface.
Remediation: Upgraded to @types/node ^22.10.0.
Verification: npm run build passes.

Finding: Dead/unused code: unused http import, unused retriesLeft parameters, unused req parameter.
Impact: Noise, misleading signatures, and no compiler guard against future dead code.
Remediation: Removed dead items; enabled noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters in tsconfig.
Verification: npm run build passes with both flags.

Finding: Generated VICIdial dialplan and .env snippet hardcoded port 533 instead of the actual PORT.
Impact: Changing PORT (or using Docker on 8080) produced Asterisk CURL/AudioSocket registration against the wrong port.
Remediation: Use process.env.PORT (validated) with 533 fallback in both the CURL URL and PORT= line.
Verification: npm run build + tests pass; generated config inspected.

Finding: Docker healthcheck targeted the old privileged port and runtime data had no persistent volume.
Impact: Container reported unhealthy; SQLite/recordings were lost on container replacement.
Remediation: Healthcheck uses 8080/health/live; VAC_DATA_DIR=/data with VOLUME and ownership.
Verification: Static review only (no Docker in sandbox); README run command updated.

Finding: Docker runtime image retained all dev dependencies after build.
Impact: Larger image and unnecessary TypeScript/test tooling in production.
Remediation: npm prune --omit=dev after build.
Verification: Static review only.

Finding: data/console-state.json (35 KB runtime state, 5 agents) was tracked and shipped, diverging from server defaults.
Impact: Every clone/ViciBox release inherited one machine's local edits; runtime state could leak into releases.
Remediation: Untracked with git rm --cached; data/ is now ignored; local file preserved.
Verification: git status shows the file deleted from the index but still present on disk.

Finding: audit/browser-results.json (212 KB generated output) was tracked.
Impact: Repository noise and stale inventory masquerading as current evidence.
Remediation: Removed and ignored; regenerate with audit/browser-smoke.cjs when Chromium is available.
Verification: git status shows deletion; .gitignore updated.

Finding: .vscode/launch.json and tasks.json hardcoded a production IP and an F:\ path; ops/set-deepgram-key.ps1 hardcoded an absolute path.
Impact: Developer tooling failed on other machines and embedded a real host address.
Remediation: Loopback host/ports, ${workspaceFolder}, node executable and $PSScriptRoot-relative project root.
Verification: Files reviewed; json/code syntax valid.

Finding: DOWNLOAD-NOTES.txt claimed build elite-2.19, 42/42+19/19 tests, a hardcoded public IP and a 100-port EADDRINUSE fallback.
Impact: Operators received false deployment/test expectations.
Remediation: Updated to nova-3.5, current test-report reference, parameterized networking and honest port behavior; Docker quick start added.
Verification: Reviewed against package.json/version.json and current server behavior.

Finding: README described Docker/Render as a port-533 root service and omitted the /data volume.
Impact: Copy-pasted Docker commands failed; data was not persisted.
Remediation: Documented unprivileged 8080 image, -p 533:8080, ADMIN_PASSWORD and named volume.
Verification: Commands match Dockerfile.

Finding: AWS deployment doc presented one IP as the release target without saying it must be replaced.
Impact: Operators could deploy against a stale/unowned address.
Remediation: Marked it as an example and told the operator to substitute their EC2 public IPv4/DNS; documented curl prerequisite and voiceagent service user.
Verification: Reviewed.

Finding: docs/AUDIT-REPORT.md was a stale 2026-10-26 prototype audit (28% readiness) presented without context.
Impact: Contradicted the current production codebase and misled readers.
Remediation: Added a HISTORICAL banner pointing to the current report.
Verification: Reviewed.

Finding: Static-site sync copies public/ to docs/ but never prunes files removed from public/.
Impact: Removed assets/handlers can remain served from GitHub Pages.
Remediation: Add a managed-file manifest and delete stale mirrored files while preserving docs-only documents.
Verification: tests/static-site-verify.ts checks mirror parity for present files, not deletion of removed files.

Finding: Server defaults create v5/4 agents (no a_jessica) while public/default-state.json and data/console-state.json are v4/5 agents.
Impact: Fresh server installs and the static/GitHub Pages demo show different bot sets; persona parity tests pin the static fixture.
Remediation: Decide the canonical seed; either add Jessica to server defaults or remove her from the demo fixture, then update tests/migrations.
Verification: tests/persona-verify.ts asserts the shipped static fixture; no failing gate, but the discrepancy is real.

Finding: speech-service/requirements-test.txt re-pins runtime packages instead of including requirements.txt.
Impact: Test environment can drift from the production image's resolved versions.
Remediation: Use -r requirements.txt plus test-only extras, with a constraints file for reproducibility.
Verification: pytest 31 passed with the current file; no functional failure.

Finding: Build identifier is manually duplicated in public/version.json, index.html CURRENT_BUILD and ?v= asset links.
Impact: A partial bump produces mixed cache-busting versions.
Remediation: Generate all three from one source at release time and add a CI parity check.
Verification: tests/static-site-verify.ts currently checks consistency of the checked-in triple.

Finding: Core gates executed on 2026-11-19 after fixes.
Evidence: npm ci, npm run build, npm test (18 suites / 120 checks), npm audit --audit-level=high, speech-service pytest
Impact: Provides executable evidence for the release claim.
Remediation: Keep gates in CI and re-run on the deployment commit.
Verification: Build 0 errors; full npm test exit 0 with 120 checks; npm audit 0 vulnerabilities; pytest 31 passed; rebuilt dist includes vici-sip-registration.js.

Finding: Docker image was not built or run.
Impact: Container-specific runtime behavior (user, volume, healthcheck) is statically reviewed only.
Remediation: Run docker build + docker run -p 533:8080 ... on the EC2 host or a Docker-capable machine.
Verification: Not executed.

Finding: deploy/aws-deploy.sh, systemd and nginx were not executed here.
Evidence: no AWS credentials/SSH and no systemd/nginx in sandbox
Impact: The EC2 path is validated by static review, bash -n and the documented runbook, not an end-to-end deploy.
Remediation: Run the script on the target EC2 instance and verify /api/health on both hops.
Verification: Not executed.

Finding: No live Deepgram, VICIdial or SIP registrar call was placed; tests use mocks.
Evidence: no provider key/PBX access in sandbox
Impact: Provider schema, real call transfer, carrier behavior and real SIP digest/NAT behavior remain unproven.
Remediation: Use a dedicated test key, an isolated ViciBox and a dedicated SIP account before production; place controlled test calls and confirm refresh/unregister.
Verification: Tests default offline; VAC_TEST_LIVE is explicit opt-in; SIP suite uses a local mock registrar only.

Finding: Chromium visual/mobile smoke was not run in this session.
Evidence: playwright-core/Chromium not installed and browser CDN is outside allowed network
Impact: Visual regressions, real viewport overflow and keyboard-only behavior were not re-measured.
Remediation: Run audit/browser-smoke.cjs with Playwright installed before a UI release.
Verification: Static-console (jsdom) tests pass; historical audit recorded 27 viewport checks.

Finding: The current session branch has no commit, no remote branch and no pull request; all audit fixes exist only in the working tree/index.
Evidence: HEAD a6f933e; branch includes merge 9e9625d of origin/main 7acd3ca; no upstream; git ls-remote has no arena/600a80f3-voice-agent-console; gh pr list --head returns []; working tree committed.
Impact: The reviewed fixes cannot be merged or deployed from the remote, and collaborators cannot see them.
Remediation: Push the branch, open a PR to main, let CI pass on the pushed commit, then merge and re-run gates on the merge commit.
Verification: Inspected git status/log/remote and gh pr list on 2026-11-19; local commit succeeded.

Finding: origin/main was 25 commits ahead; PR #47 (VICIdial three-mode SIP connector) was not covered by the original audit.
Evidence: origin/main 7acd3ca merged into the session branch as 9e9625d; PR #47 reviewed in report section 11.
Impact: Resolved for this branch: SIP and bridge integration are now built and tested together.
Remediation: Merged origin/main, audited the new SIP connector, hardened it, rebuilt dist and reran all gates.
Verification: npm run build exit 0; npm test exit 0 (18 suites/120 checks); SIP suite 7/7; live smoke on 127.0.0.1:5544.

Finding: origin/main committed dist was stale: it had no dist/vici-sip-registration.js and dist/vici-bridge.js did not import SipRegistrationClient.
Evidence: a6f933e adds dist/vici-sip-registration.js and rebuilds dist/vici-bridge.js with the import.
Impact: Resolved locally; npm start on this commit runs the new SIP registration path.
Remediation: Rebuilt and committed dist; recommend a CI check that rebuilds and fails on dist drift.
Verification: npm run build exit 0; grep confirms require("./vici-sip-registration") in dist/vici-bridge.js.

Finding: The GitHub Pages deployment workflow on main fails at Configure Pages because GitHub Pages is not enabled for the repository.
Evidence: Run 44448830794 build step "Configure Pages" failed; GET /repos/muneeb819/Voice-Agent-Console/pages returns 404; Product CI on the same SHA succeeded.
Impact: The static demo is not published by GitHub Actions even though the static mirror and tests pass.
Remediation: Enable Pages with the GitHub Actions source (or disable/remove the Pages workflow if Vercel is the intended static host).
Verification: gh run list / gh api inspection on 2026-11-19.

Finding: PR #47's SIP registrar client had no automated coverage and was absent from the test runner.
Evidence: src/vici-sip-registration.ts; tests/ had no SIP suite; tools/run-tests.js omitted it.
Impact: Digest auth, refresh, unregister and failure paths could regress silently in the telephony path.
Remediation: Added tests/sip-registration-verify.ts with a mock UDP registrar and the sip-registration runner step.
Verification: node tools/run-tests.js sip-registration: 7/7 pass; included in npm test (18 suites, 120 checks).

Finding: SIP registrar/domain/username/auth-username/bridge-host values were interpolated into raw UDP headers without validation.
Evidence: src/vici-sip-registration.ts sendRegister/authHeader; src/defaults.ts normalizeState accepted arbitrary strings.
Impact: CRLF/header injection, malformed Contact/Via/From values and URI parameter confusion from imported state or direct callers.
Remediation: Allowlist cleanSipHost/cleanSipUser in normalizeState; defensive header/URI rejection in start(); quote-escape and bound digest challenge values.
Verification: SIP suite asserts CRLF/header inputs fail closed, imported values are stripped, and digest 401/200 lifecycle works.

Finding: Registration advertised the saved sipPort even when BRIDGE_SIP_PORT changed the actual listener port.
Evidence: src/vici-bridge.ts start() read getConsoleState().vici directly before constructing SipRegistrationClient.
Impact: A registrar would route calls to a closed/mismatched port after an environment override.
Remediation: Pass { ...getConsoleState().vici, sipPort: this.sipPort } to the client so Contact/Via use the bound port.
Verification: Code review and successful build; not exercised against a real registrar.

Finding: Loopback or 0.0.0.0 Bridge Host was accepted for registration, producing an unreachable or ambiguous Contact.
Impact: Registration can silently fail or advertise an internal address to the registrar.
Remediation: Client rejects loopback/unspecified Bridge Host; deployment preflight reports an error before startup.
Verification: SIP suite checks loopback rejection and preflight error item.

Finding: Repeated 401/407 responses caused unbounded re-authentication attempts.
Impact: A misconfigured credential or hostile registrar could drive a UDP request storm and CPU load.
Remediation: Added authAttempts; fail closed after more than two consecutive challenges.
Verification: SIP suite sends repeated 401s and asserts exactly three requests then failed status.

Finding: stop() could throw when the UDP socket never bound and emitted a duplicate unregister request.
Evidence: src/vici-sip-registration.ts stop() called sendRegister(0) twice and socket.close without guarding.
Impact: Bridge shutdown could reject or leave a partially stopped service.
Remediation: Exception-safe socket close; removed the second Expires: 0 send.
Verification: SIP lifecycle test completes cleanly; code review of the guarded close.

Finding: Authenticated SIP status exposes the registrar host and bounded lastError text.
Impact: Viewer-role users learn the registrar address and failure details; no password or digest material is exposed.
Remediation: Decide whether to redact the registrar for non-admin roles.
Verification: Code review; SIP suite confirms no password appears in requests.

Finding: The SIP password is not sent in REGISTER requests and is not resolvable through provider placeholders.
Evidence: src/vici-sip-registration.ts authHeader uses a digest response; src/env-store.ts provider allowlist excludes VICI_SIP_PASSWORD.
Impact: Confirms the credential remains server-side.
Remediation: Keep the account dedicated; rotate it if the registrar is compromised.
Verification: SIP suite asserts no password substring and Authorization Digest fields; provider interpolation test returns empty.

Finding: SIP mode/registrar/credential/Bridge Host changes are read at bridge startup; no live re-register action exists.
Impact: Operators must restart the console, dropping active calls, to apply SIP changes.
Remediation: UI now states the restart requirement; add a controlled restart/re-register action if needed.
Verification: Static-site/static-console suites pass with the updated note.

Finding: Real operator IPs were hard-coded in UI placeholders, status text, .env.example, deploy comments, the ViciBox runbook and AWS deployment docs.
Evidence: public/app.js (192.168.18.29, 115.186.137.240); .env.example; deploy/aws-deploy.sh; deploy/vicibox-install.sh; VICIBOX-PRODUCTION-RUNBOOK.md; docs/AWS-DEPLOYMENT.md; README.md (3.107.192.118).
Impact: Wrong-target configuration and unnecessary disclosure of production addresses in a public repo.
Remediation: Replaced with 127.0.0.1, YOUR-BRIDGE-HOST, <BRIDGE_PUBLIC_IP>, <VICIBOX_PUBLIC_IP> and <EC2_PUBLIC_IP>; synced docs/app.js.
Verification: grep finds no old operator IPs in public/app.js, runbook, AWS docs, src or deploy scripts; static-site suite passed.
